Create a professional character reference sheet based strictly on <image1>.

The character is the same person shown in <image2>. Use <image2> as an additional reference to capture more accurate facial features, proportions, hairstyle, clothing details, accessories, and other fine details.

Character consistency:
* Preserve the character's exact face, facial structure, hairstyle, proportions, clothing, colors, accessories, and identifiable details from the references.
* Do not redesign, reinterpret, beautify, or alter the face.
* Maintain the exact same person and identity across every panel.
* Capture all fine details from both reference images.
* Use <image2> whenever it provides additional information or details not clearly visible in <image1>.

Top section — full-body turnaround:
Place three full-body character views across the top:
1. Front view
2. Side/profile view
3. Back view
* Same outfit and identical character proportions in all three views.
* Use the same neutral standing pose for every view.
* Arms slightly separated from the torso so the silhouette and clothing are clearly visible.
* Hands relaxed and naturally posed.
* Keep the camera height, framing, scale, and perspective consistent between all three views.
* No pose drift, proportion drift, outfit changes, or character redesign.
* The back view must accurately match the front and side views.

Bottom section — expressions and props:
Use the bottom area for a clean collection of smaller reference panels.
Include three facial expression close-ups:
* Open mouth
* Smiling with teeth visible
* Surprised expression

Right side — large portrait:
Place one large, highly detailed shoulder-up portrait of the same person on the right side.
* Preserve the exact face and identity from <image1> and <image2>.
* Use <image2> to improve facial accuracy and capture details that may be missing from <image1>.
* High facial detail and accurate proportions.
* Clean, centered composition.
* Professional character-sheet presentation.
* The portrait must clearly match the face shown in all turnaround views and expression panels.

Layout and quality:
* Clean, professional character-sheet layout.
* Clearly separated panels with consistent spacing.
* Nothing may overlap, collide, merge, or bleed into another panel.
* No element should cross into another frame.
* Keep every character, expression, prop, and portrait completely contained within its designated area.
* No cropped heads, hands, feet, props, or important clothing details.
* Balanced spacing and clear visual hierarchy.
* High resolution and highly detailed.
* Maintain absolute character consistency across the entire sheet.
* Zero identity drift, zero outfit drift, zero proportion drift, and zero visual inconsistency.

{"version": 1, "content": "


Qwen Image Edit 2.1 — Wildcard Guide

Wildcards expand into detailed editing prompts. Type __qwen21/<name>__ for a specific edit, or __qwen21/*__ for a random one. You can mix wildcards with your own text — the wildcard is replaced inline before the prompt is sent.

<image1>, <image2>, <image3> inside a wildcard refer to the reference images connected to the node, in order.

Available edits

WildcardImgsWhat it does
__qwen21/sheet__1Quick character sheet: front, side, back + headshot
__qwen21/prosheet__1Pro reference sheet, image2 as extra ref
__qwen21/newscene__1Subject into a new random scene (location wildcard)
__qwen21/backgroundswap__2Subject of image1 onto background of image2
__qwen21/enhance__1Detail enhance, restore, creative upscale (pairs with detailer LoRA)
__qwen21/faceswap__2Face of image1 ← identity from image2
__qwen21/headswap__2Head+hair of image1 ← head from image2
__qwen21/eyeswap__2Eyes of image1 ← eyes from image2
__qwen21/makeupswap__2Makeup, contacts & lipstick of image2 onto image1 — identity kept
__qwen21/hairswap__2Hair of image1 ← hair from image2
__qwen21/outfitswap__2Dresses subject of image1 with outfit from image2
__qwen21/poseswap__2Subject of image1 into body pose from image2
__qwen21/expressionswap__2Expression of image2 onto image1
__qwen21/multiref__3Scene combining image1 + image2 inside image3
__qwen21/multiedit__1Applies every edit you describe at once
__qwen21/timeweather__1Change time/weather to what you describe
__qwen21/removeobject__1Removes the object you name + inpaint
__qwen21/insertobject__1Inserts the object you describe
__qwen21/textedit__1Replaces visible text with yours
__qwen21/novelview__1Camera angle you describe
__qwen21/anime2real__1Anime → photorealistic human
__qwen21/real2anime__1Photo → manhwa/webtoon illustration

⚠️ Important: QwenVL bypass

The __qwen21/*__ editing wildcards are already complete edit instructions (they contain <image1>/<image2> bindings). The QwenVL Unified node is bypassed in this workflow so the expanded text reaches the encoder untouched — if the LLM rewrote it, the image bindings would break and the edit would fail. When generating images instead of editing, un-bypass it with Ctrl+B: the LLM then expands your text and content wildcards (__pmp/...__) into a full prompt via the selected preset (e.g. Pony→Natural). Keep it bypassed (or set passthrough = true) whenever an edit wildcard is in the prompt.

Tips

  • Mind the image count — edits marked 2 or 3 need that many references, in the right order (e.g. faceswap: image1 = photo to modify, image2 = identity donor).
  • Edits that need a target — for removeobject, insertobject, textedit, novelview, timeweather and multiedit, describe what to change in your own words next to the wildcard: a red parked car, __qwen21/removeobject__.
  • Combine with text — __qwen21/backgroundswap__, dramatic mood works fine.
  • Add your own — drop a .txt in ComfyUI/models/wildcards/, one prompt per line → becomes __filename__. YAML supports nested keys like __name/subkey__.
  • Random pick — __qwen21/*__ chooses a random edit, fun for batch runs.
